GlobalPolicy.redaction: API keys truncated (first 4 chars only) in all env var logs
GlobalPolicy.autonomy-gate: Pipeline must produce at least one FINAL transcript per 60s window to be considered functional.

VF-OUTGOING.NAME: OutgoingTranslationRUtoEN
VF-OUTGOING.scenario: User speaks Russian into Jabra mic, remote hears English via meeting app

VF-INCOMING.NAME: IncomingTranslationENtoRU
VF-INCOMING.scenario: Remote speaks English, captured via CABLE Output, user hears Russian

VF-FALLBACK-STT.NAME: STTFallback
VF-FALLBACK-STT.scenario: Deepgram WS drops (error 10054), pipeline falls back to Whisper
VF-FALLBACK-STT.expected-outcome: After 3 Deepgram drops, UnifiedSttSession switches to Whisper
VF-FALLBACK-STT.failure-expected: Deepgram WS drops every ~20-25s on unstable networks

VF-FALLBACK-TRANSLATION.NAME: TranslationFallback
VF-FALLBACK-TRANSLATION.scenario: Groq fails, falls back to LiteLLM, then Yandex

VF-AUDIO.NAME: AudioCaptureStability
VF-AUDIO.scenario: Both pipelines capture audio without WASAPI errors
VF-AUDIO.expected-outcome: CAPTURE batches with speech-level rms (>0.05) on outgoing pipeline
VF-AUDIO.failure-expected: 0x800706CC when WASAPI COM held by list_devices()

VF-CONFIG.NAME: SettingsPersistence
VF-CONFIG.scenario: User changes device/API settings in Flask UI, pipeline restarts with new config
VF-CONFIG.expected-outcome: settings.json updated, Elixir passes env vars to Rust, pipelines use new config

VF-LATENCY-BASELINE.NAME: LatencyBaselineCapture
VF-LATENCY-BASELINE.scenario: Collect per-stage latency on the current pipeline before and after each wave.
VF-LATENCY-BASELINE.expected-outcome: Each utterance yields comparable STT, translation, TTS, and total timings with provider attribution.

VF-LOCAL-FIRST.NAME: LocalFirstPipelineRUEN
VF-LOCAL-FIRST.scenario: Run the ru/en path with local STT and local MT, without relying on Deepgram, Groq, LiteLLM, or Yandex on the hot path.
VF-LOCAL-FIRST.expected-outcome: Both pipelines produce transcript, translation, and TTS events in local-only mode.

VF-INCREMENTAL-PARTIALS.NAME: IncrementalPartials
VF-INCREMENTAL-PARTIALS.scenario: Stable partial transcripts are emitted before final utterance completion and can trigger early downstream work.
VF-INCREMENTAL-PARTIALS.expected-outcome: UI and logs observe stable partials earlier than final transcript markers.

scenarios.scenario-2: Piper TTS produces audio for Russian text (incoming)
scenarios.scenario-3: TTS preload timeout — ONNX model file missing

scenarios.scenario-1: Outgoing pipeline captures speech (rms>0.05) from Jabra mic
scenarios.scenario-2: Incoming pipeline captures from CABLE Output

scenarios.scenario-2: Live transcript SSE stream shows [STT]/[TR]/[TOTAL] events

scenarios.scenario-1: Realtime endpointing values are reduced and visible in STT connection logs.
scenarios.scenario-2: Translation fallback returns the first successful provider instead of waiting through serial retries.
scenarios.scenario-3: Per-utterance latency logs include provider attribution for comparison against baseline.
scenarios.scenario-4: Realtime profile still waits on long retries or long translation timeouts.

scenarios.scenario-1: Persistent local STT operates without temp WAV roundtrips or per-utterance worker launch.
scenarios.scenario-2: Local ru→en and en→ru translation works through the integrated local provider.
scenarios.scenario-3: Audio playback follows the fast local path without waiting for cloud correction.
scenarios.scenario-4: The local-first preset still attempts cloud providers on the critical path.

scenarios.scenario-1: Stable partial transcripts appear before final transcript completion.
scenarios.scenario-2: Stale translation and TTS jobs are canceled or dropped rather than accumulating backlog.
scenarios.scenario-3: Playback starts from confirmed translated segments before full-utterance completion on long phrases.
scenarios.scenario-4: Incremental mode causes repeated retranslations of the same prefix or duplicated playback.

Gate-Phase-1.name: Foundation
Gate-Phase-1.goal: Both pipelines compile, start, and produce at least one transcript within 60s

commands.command-3: Start engine, verify pipeline_trace.log shows both pipelines running

required-evidence.evidence-1: [outgoing] STT TRANSCRIPT appears within 60s of pipeline start
required-evidence.evidence-2: [incoming] STT TRANSCRIPT appears within 60s of remote audio capture No 0x800706CC errors

Gate-Phase-2.name: Full Pipeline
Gate-Phase-2.goal: End-to-end translation works in both directions with TTS output

commands.command-1: Speak Russian → verify English TTS plays via CABLE Input
commands.command-2: Speak English on remote device → verify Russian TTS plays via Jabra

required-evidence.evidence-3: Both pipelines produce at least 3 translations per test run

Gate-Latency-W1.name: FastLatencyRelief
Gate-Latency-W1.goal: Current pipeline tail latency is reduced without loss of end-to-end functionality.

commands.command-3: Run both pipelines and compare per-stage latency logs against baseline

required-evidence.evidence-1: Updated STT endpointing values appear in connection logs
required-evidence.evidence-2: provider_used markers are present on translation path
required-evidence.evidence-3: p95 translate latency improves on degraded-network comparison runs

Gate-Latency-W2.name: LocalFirstCriticalPath
Gate-Latency-W2.goal: ru/en dual pipeline operates end-to-end in local-first mode without cloud dependency on the hot path.

commands.command-3: Run both pipelines with local-first preset and verify transcript, translation, and TTS markers

required-evidence.evidence-2: Both directions emit transcript and TTS markers without external API availability
required-evidence.evidence-3: Audio output follows the local path without waiting for cloud correction

Gate-Latency-W3.name: IncrementalStreamingArchitecture
Gate-Latency-W3.goal: Stable partials and early playback reduce perceived response time below full-utterance latency.

commands.command-3: Run long-phrase tests and verify partial, stable-partial, and early-audio markers

required-evidence.evidence-1: Stable partial markers appear before final transcript markers
required-evidence.evidence-3: Playback begins before full utterance completion on long phrases
